script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for March 24. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Right now, your skin is sensing: the pressure of your clothes, the temperature of the air, the texture of anything you're touching.  Millions of sensors, constantly reporting.  Skin is your largest organ—and your most constant source of information about the world.

Your skin covers about 20 square feet and weighs around 8 pounds. It's not just a wrapper—it's an active organ that senses, regulates temperature, produces vitamin D, and defends against pathogens. Skin is doing more than you know. Your fingertips have about 2,500 touch receptors per square centimeter—the highest density anywhere on your body.  That's why you can read Braille, thread a needle, or detect vibrations too subtle for other body parts.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Connection requires contact.  Touch reminds us that we're physical beings in a physical world—and that our understanding grows through direct encounter.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Touch Awareness - Feel What You're Feeling.

Here's your activity: For the next minute, close your eyes and notice everything your skin is sensing—pressure, temperature, textures, air movement. We often ignore this constant stream of information. What is your skin telling you right now? This helps you increase awareness of tactile experience.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how skin feels things can be applied to touch awareness - feel what you're feeling. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
